result.title: Compact Motion Embeddings for Feed-forward Unified Human Animation
result.summary: Animating a reference image with a driver's motion requires a motion representation that captures face, hand, and body articulation but excludes the driver's appearance. Most body animation methods take motion from external pose estimators and render it with many denoising steps; compact learned motion representations mostly cover the face. We present FUHA, a real-time-capable feed-forward transformer that learns a compact motion embedding of the whole human and uses it for face, upper-body, and full-body animation. A Q-Former compresses the driver's features from a frozen visual encoder into this embedding. To disentangle motion from appearance, a novel contrastive loss pulls it toward the motion embedding of the driver's rendered keypoint image and away from that of the same person in another pose. At inference time, FUHA needs no external pose estimators, keypoints, or parametric body models. As a retrieval key, the motion embedding matches body pose better than the learned global embeddings of ten vision encoders. Its same-person retrieval rate is 0.1%, against 9.5% for its own DINOv3 backbone. On our upper-body benchmark, FUHA outperforms all baselines on every self-reenactment metric and on cross-reenactment identity similarity. It is competitive on face and full-body and runs at up to 38.9 FPS at 512x512 on a single RTX 4090.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FUHA 前馈 transformer 人体动画框架：用 Q-Former 将冻结视觉编码器提取的驱动特征压缩为紧凑 motion embedding，并以对比损失使其与外观解耦，从而无需外部姿态估计即可实时驱动人脸、半身与全身。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「视觉特征压成定长 latent + 对比损失剔除身份外观」的训练思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态如何保留任务必要视觉信息、抑制无关内容，以及用检索式指标诊断 latent 中信息泄漏；但论文任务是动画生成，与推理状态生成无直接关系。
